content: Example services use the vanilla org.openapi.generator plugin with generatorName=spring, interfaceOnly=true, useSpringBoot3=true, useTags=true, skipDefaultInterface=true. The spec generates *Api interfaces + DTO models; we write the @RestController impls. Generated sources go to build/generated and are wired into the main source set; compileJava dependsOn openApiGenerate. Keep spec <-> controllers <-> DTOs in sync.

name: Hierarchical REST paths mirror the resource tree
description: Nest URLs to reflect the resource hierarchy: /catalogs/{id}/categories/{id}/products/{id}. Validate each ancestor exists and that the child belongs to it (findByIdAndParentId) so cross-parent access returns 404, not someone else's data. This nesting is also what the ABAC hierarchical-authorization pattern keys off.

content: Map JPA column types to match the entity exactly, validated against REAL Postgres. char(3) becomes bpchar and fails Hibernate ddl-auto=validate against a String field expecting varchar — use varchar(n). timestamptz needs @TimeZoneStorage(NATIVE) on OffsetDateTime. Run schema validation under Testcontainers (real Postgres), never H2, so these mismatches surface in the build.

name: REST API conventions + design-review baseline (both example services)
description: Both example services share one REST convention set, now pinned in docs/guides/REST-API-DESIGN.md + reviewed in docs/code-review/REST-API-DESIGN-REVIEW.md. Conventions: spec-first OpenAPI (org.openapi.generator, interfaceOnly, controller implements <Api>); /api/v1 path versioning; plural nouns; ownership-nesting <=3 levels (catalog->category->product hits 3); custom op as noun sub-resource (POST /teams/{id}/transfer-ownership); PUT-not-PATCH full-replace; ApiError{status,message,timestamp} as application/json. Status rules: 400=Bean-Validation/syntax, 422=domain-rule (tag dict / role-subset), 409=state-conflict/immutable, 503=fail-closed dependency outage (tag dict unreachable -> reject, never store untagged), no 401 (gateway authenticates; deny=403). Authz per endpoint = one of three: type-level @OpaPreAuthorize, load-then-check (only getCategory, because tags live only on CategoryEntity), partial-eval list filter (empty list not full table on no-grant). Public/internal split: /api/v1/** authenticated; /internal/** permitAll BUT network-isolated, never gateway-fronted (deployment invariant, not code). REVIEW VERDICT: consistent, no fail-open found. Gaps=maturity targets, not bugs: (1 Medium) no RFC-7807 problem+json / stable errorCode -> top publication item; (2 Low) no Location on 201; (3) getCatalog/getProduct annotation-only vs getCategory load-then-check is intentional (doc it); (4) some user-svc mutations (UserController, POST /teams) authenticated-but-not-ABAC-gated = bootstrap seam, add intent comments; (5) no pagination = documented demo limit; (6) no actions/pageActions = Phase 6 action-enrichment.

title: Phase 5.9 error contract: RFC-7807 problem+json + library-owned errorCode vocabulary (ADR 0011)
rationale: Settled via grill-me 2026-06-09 and pinned by ADR 0011. Five forks: (1) depth = the minimal additive RFC-7807 superset (type/title/status/detail/instance + errorCode/timestamp extensions), NO hosted type registry. (2) clean replacement of the legacy ApiError status/message/timestamp shape, message renamed to detail, content type flips to application/problem+json (no external consumers pre-publication, so a clean break is free). (3) vocabulary = an ApiErrorCode INTERFACE plus a LibraryErrorCode enum in opa-abac-spring-security for the failures the library raises, each example service ships its OWN enum implementing the same interface (a Java enum cannot be subclassed, so the contract slot is the interface). (4) SEMANTIC granularity: one code per distinct client-actionable failure, not one per HTTP status. (5) errorCode is a first-class TYPED enum member of each spec ProblemDetail schema so the generated client is typed, which is why the library ships its own small ProblemDetail DTO rather than Spring built-in ProblemDetail whose properties map is untyped. A non-obvious real-code catch the slice-planner surfaced: 403 from OpaPreAuthorize is rendered by Spring Security default today, so the T1 advice base must explicitly map AccessDeniedException to ACCESS_DENIED 403 or 403s never become problem+json. Pagination split to its OWN slice Phase 5.95 sequenced 5.9 then 5.95 then Phase 6 so action enrichment lands on an already-paginated 7807-clean surface. Out of scope: hosted registry, actions metadata (Phase 6), any authorization behavior change.

name: Library-owned RFC-7807 error vocabulary: ApiErrorCode interface + per-app enum + shared advice base
description: Phase 5.9 T1. The error contract is published as a library-owned, extensible, typed vocabulary in opa-abac-spring-security. A Java enum cannot be subclassed, so the shared contract is an ApiErrorCode INTERFACE (code, default problemType deriving /problems/kebab, default title) and the library ships LibraryErrorCode enum implementing it for the failures it raises or generic ones (ACCESS_DENIED 403, DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE 503, VALIDATION_FAILED 400, RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND 404, STATE_CONFLICT 409, TAG_VALUE_ILLEGAL and ROLE_SUBSET_VIOLATION 422). Each app ships its OWN enum implementing the same interface for domain failures; granularity is semantic (one code per distinct client-actionable failure, not one per status). Carry the HttpStatus ON the enum constant so the advice resolves status-plus-code from one source. Three reuse seams: (1) ProblemDetail is the library's OWN record carrier, NOT Spring org.springframework.http.ProblemDetail whose untyped properties map would lose the typed errorCode in the OpenAPI schema; (2) ProblemDetailFactory builds the body and a problem+json ResponseEntity with no decision logic; (3) AbstractProblemAdvice is the RestControllerAdvice base each app advice extends and it carries the AccessDeniedException plus AuthorizationDeniedException to 403 ACCESS_DENIED mapping. That last seam is load-bearing: a 403 from OpaPreAuthorize or OpaAuthorizationManager is rendered by Spring Security default, NOT the per-app advice, so without the shared base 403s never become problem+json. The mapping renders an already-decided deny, it never authorizes (no fail-open).

name: Per-service problem+json adoption: extend the library advice base, replace ApiError in the spec, Location on 201
description: Phase 5.9 T2 (catalog; T3 mirrors for user-svc). A service adopts the library error contract in one self-contained module commit: (1) its @RestControllerAdvice extends AbstractProblemAdvice from opa-abac-spring-security and each @ExceptionHandler resolves its exception to an ApiErrorCode (a LibraryErrorCode where the failure is generic, a service-own enum constant only where a client branches WITHIN a status beyond the library codes) then builds a ProblemDetail via the inherited problem() helper, pulling instance from an injected HttpServletRequest; the SAME HTTP status as before is preserved per exception. (2) The OpenAPI spec REMOVES the old ApiError schema and adds a ProblemDetail schema whose errorCode is a TYPED enum = the union of codes that service emits; error responses flip content to application/problem+json; declare reusable Forbidden/UnprocessableEntity/ServiceUnavailable responses and wire the 422/503 onto the operations that raise them so the contract documents the real surface. Codegen regenerates the model and drift is a build break: on a CLEAN regeneration ApiError.java disappears (no schema -> no model) and ProblemDetail.java gains a typed ErrorCodeEnum. (3) Every 201 emits Location via ServletUriComponentsBuilder.fromCurrentRequest().path('/{id}').buildAndExpand(savedId) returning ResponseEntity.created(location); nested collection paths are correct by construction since they extend the actual request URI. The build-breaker (removing ApiError regenerates the model) is confined to that one module and lands in the same commit; the per-app enum may be empty when every failure maps to a library code (do not invent codes). Proof: a full-context MockMvc IT against real Postgres asserts problem+json + the right errorCode + no legacy message per status, and Location on a 201; a denied-403 path is proven by the library unit test (the inherited AccessDeniedException mapping) plus the live e2e, since a permissive test chain cannot drive a deny.

title: ApiErrorCode carries status(); the conflict group splits per client-actionable failure
rationale: Phase 5.9 T3. Two refinements emerged adopting the contract in the richer user-service. (1) GRANULARITY: the user-service advice grouped six exceptions under one 409 and two under 422. Per ADR 0011 §4 we split the 409 group into distinct UserMgmtErrorCode constants a client would handle differently (TEAM_TARGET_EXISTS, MEMBERSHIP_CONFLICT, ROLE_CODE_CONFLICT, ROLE_IMMUTABLE, TAG_KEY_CONFLICT, TAG_DEFINITION_IMMUTABLE) and gave the bad-shape tag-def its own 422 code (TAG_DEFINITION_INVALID); the subset rule reuses the library ROLE_SUBSET_VIOLATION and not-found/validation reuse library codes. So the catalog enum ended up empty (all failures generic) while the user-service enum has seven app codes — granularity is driven by how many distinct failures a client branches on, not by service. (2) The contract slot is COMPLETED by carrying HttpStatus status() on the ApiErrorCode INTERFACE (not just the concrete enums). Then AbstractProblemAdvice exposes a single problem(ApiErrorCode, detail, request) overload that reads code.status() for any code — library or app — so per-app advices drop the per-code-status helper boilerplate entirely and just route exception -> code. An empty app enum (CatalogErrorCode) implements status() with an unreachable throw since it has no constants. Location on 201 is keyed by the resource's ADDRESSABLE identifier from the DTO (userId for a membership whose GET path is /members/{userId}, code for a role-def, key for a tag-def) built via ServletUriComponentsBuilder.fromCurrentRequest().path, not the surrogate row id; entities here expose no getId() so the DTO is the id source. The deny 403 is provable end-to-end in a real secured IT (a subject with no team role hits a gated mutation -> in-process OPA returns no role-def -> deny -> the inherited AccessDeniedException mapping renders ACCESS_DENIED problem+json), which is stronger than the catalog case where the permissive test chain can only prove 403 via a unit test.

title: Phase 5.95 pagination: exact-count envelope + Pageable seam + determinism by construction (ADR 0012)
rationale: Settled via grill-me 2026-06-11, pinned by ADR 0012 + PAGINATION-ENVELOPE/00-DESIGN. Forks closed: (1) exact-count {count,page,perPage,items} on ALL four AbacQueryService paths - the allowlist fallback is already fetch-all, so paging its in-memory filtered result costs nothing new and keeps count exact (rejected Slice/hasNext and count:null hybrid); (2) Spring-native seam - additive findAuthorized(...,Pageable)->Page<T> overload, wire envelope owned by the OpenAPI specs (PageEnvelope + <Resource>Page allOf, shared page/perPage params; rejected library-owned envelope type as mediator-worldview); (3) strict 0-based params: defaults 0/20, bounds 1..100, 400 VALIDATION_FAILED (no clamping), past-the-end = 200+empty+exact count (last page is subject-relative under ABAC, never 404); (4) determinism by construction: fixed createdAt ASC,id ASC on all 9 endpoints, the paged overload THROWS on unsorted Pageable, fallback fetches candidates SQL-sorted so both paths page the same sequence; client sort deferred; (5) envelope-everywhere/authz-nowhere: all 9 public lists, zero authorization change (only listCategories stays residual-filtered), /internal/** unpaginated by design, clean wire break, zero Rego changes.

name: OpenAPI list envelope under vanilla codegen: per-spec PageEnvelope + allOf <Resource>Page + shared param components
description: Ship one list envelope {count,page,perPage,items} across many endpoints with VANILLA org.openapi.generator (no custom templates): a 3-field PageEnvelope schema (count int64, page, perPage; required; bounds as schema constraints) + a thin allOf composition per resource (CategoryPage = PageEnvelope + required typed items) — the generator FLATTENS allOf into one model class with fluent setters, so controllers map Page<T> -> new CategoryPage().count(totalElements).page(getNumber()).perPage(getSize()).items(mapped). page/perPage as shared components/parameters (bounds live once per spec); generated @Min/@Max on @RequestParam + the interface-level @Validated surface violations as jakarta ConstraintViolationException (AOP method validation — NOT HandlerMethodValidationException; map it in the problem-advice to 400 VALIDATION_FAILED). Define the envelope base PER SPEC FILE (no cross-file $ref — it couples the two services' builds). Strict contract: 0-based page == PageRequest.of directly, no clamping, past-the-end = 200 + empty + exact count (never 404 — under ABAC the last page is subject-relative). The spec change is the build-breaker: regenerated list signatures break controllers + list-asserting tests — land all of it in that service's own commit.

name: Domain-contract fields stay out of OpenAPI schema constraints when the API pins a uniform 422
description: When a request field belongs to a domain validation contract that must answer 422 with a typed errorCode (e.g. roleLevel in the 6.5 authoring contract -> ROLE_DEFINITION_INVALID), do NOT make it schema-required or a schema enum: bean validation / Jackson enum deserialization intercepts missing/off-enum values as 400 VALIDATION_FAILED before the service runs, fragmenting one contract into two statuses. Document REQUIRED + allowed values in the property description and enforce in the service - one gate, one violation shape. Also matters because internal/bootstrap paths bypass generated DTO constraints entirely, so the service check is the only one that holds everywhere.

name: 204-op produces fix: empty application/json content, schema-less, at the spec
description: A 204-only OpenAPI operation whose error responses are application/problem+json generates produces={problem+json} only, so Spring content negotiation 406s a bare 'Accept: application/json' BEFORE the handler runs (json is NOT compatible with problem+json under the suffix rules). Fix at the spec (spec-first, never a Java produces override): declare an empty success content 'application/json: {}' — a media type with NO schema — via a shared components/responses/NoContent. The schema-less declaration widens the generated produces to {application/json, problem+json} while keeping the generated return type ResponseEntity<Void>; giving it any schema would flip the return type to Object and break every controller override. Proven by a negative-control run: the same IT fails 406→204 against the pre-fix spec, and a no-Accept request passes both ways (never was broken).

name: Unique-key lookup filter on a list endpoint: one-item page + both-or-400, via a shared onePage helper
description: A single-resource lookup keyed by a unique attribute is an OPTIONAL exact-match query filter on the list endpoint (GET /users?subject=, GET /teams?targetType=&targetId=), never a by-<key> sub-path. Semantics pinned suite-wide (REST-API-DESIGN §7): present -> a one-item page in the ADR-0012 envelope (count 0 or 1; a window past the match follows the normal past-the-end rule — content only on page 0, exact count either way, so the row never repeats across pages); unmatched -> empty page, never 404, never a full-list fallthrough; a composite pair is all-or-nothing (exactly one param -> 400 VALIDATION_FAILED thrown BEFORE any repository access — an XOR guard, blank string counts as absent); absent -> the byte-for-byte unchanged paged findAll (additive guard branch, never a replacement). Implementation: one package-private PageDefaults.onePage(Optional<T>, PageRequest) encodes the envelope semantics once (PageImpl keeps the given total when content is empty); the 400 rides IllegalArgumentException -> the existing VALIDATION_FAILED advice — no new error code, handler, or exception type.
